paper.title: ollama v0.40.17
paper.abstract: Inkling 2 Mini Inkling 2 Mini from Thinking Machines is a 26B parameter model with 5.4B active. Its looped layers give it more computation per token than its size suggests, and it still fits on a Mac at about 20GB. It handles text and images, tool calls, and thinking, and scores 79.2% on SWE-Bench Verified). ollama run inkling-2-mini Note: inkling-2-mini is supported on Apple silicon only in this release. PC support will follow in an upcoming release. What's Changed ollama launch claude supports Claude Code's deferred tool loading, so MCP tools are loaded when needed instead of all at once Ollama on Apple silicon now serves multiple requests at once. ollama launch opencode sets thinking options from the model's metadata ollama launch pi refreshes Pi's model list after sign-in and passes along prompt arguments ollama launch chatgpt --restore asks before switching an active profile and preserves existing settings and chat history; quitting ChatGPT yourself now lets it exit through its own quit prompt Running ollama with no arguments in a non-interactive shell prints help instead of erroring Ctrl+C or Ctrl+G while in a multiline """ block leaves multiline mode instead of swallowing the next line Changing the context shift setting no longer reloads the model Vulkan now uses mmap for integrated GPUs, fixing Failed to allocate pinned memory load failures on shared-memory GPUs On Windows iGPUs, partially offloaded models no longer fail to allocate the KV cache Tool definitions passed through the API keep JSON schema keywords Ollama doesn't model instead of dropping them Disabling thinking now maps to the model's lowest supported reasoning level rather than being ignored Source builds can use prebuilt MLX-C and XGrammar binaries Full Changelog : v0.40.16...v0.40.17-rc3

paper.title: Release v5.24.0
paper.abstract: Release v5.24.0 New Model additions Inkling 2 Mini Inkling 2 Mini is a multimodal model from Thinking Machines Lab that accepts text and image inputs and generates text outputs. It is a smaller sibling of Inkling 2 Small, added in v5.23.0. It has 24 decoder layers instead of 48, and compensates with a looping mechanism in which layers 6 to 17 run three times. A learned message-passing mechanism mixes the residuals of the previous pass into the attention and mixture-of-experts inputs of each loop layer. The decoder has a hidden size of 2304 and routes each token to 8 of 128 experts. The image encoder, tokenizer and processor are the same as Inkling 2 Small's. A research checkpoint ( TML-d24-varloop-research ) has the same architecture but supports a variable number of loop passes. Fewer passes are faster, and more passes improve quality. Both checkpoints contain NVFP4 and MXFP8 quantized layers, which are dequantized at load time. Links: Documentation | Blog Post | HF Blog Post Add Inkling2 Mini ( #51050 ) by @guarin Apertus 1.5 Apertus 1.5 is a multimodal model from the Swiss AI Initiative that accepts text, images and audio and generates text. It extends the Apertus language model with the EMU3.5 vision tokenizer for images and WavTokenizer for audio. The EMU3.5 tokenizer is an image-only VQGAN with the same encoder as Chameleon's, and it assigns codes by the largest inner product with the codebook. The media tokenizers turn images and audio into discrete tokens, which the language backbone processes alongside text in a shared input vocabulary. The output vocabulary contains only text tokens, so image and audio generation are not supported. Links: Documentation Apertus 1.5: add model ( #47662 ) by @RaphaelKreft WavTokenizer WavTokenizer encodes 24 kHz mono audio into discrete tokens using a single codebook, at 40 or 75 tokens per second depending on the checkpoint, and reconstructs audio from those tokens. WavTokenizerModel encodes and decodes, and WavTokenizerEncoderModel only encodes. Speech, music/audio and unified checkpoints are available. The 40-token-per-second variant is the audio tokenizer of Apertus 1.5. Training the codec is not supported. Links: Documentation | Paper Apertus 1.5: add model ( #47662 ) by @RaphaelKreft Dory Dory is a looped (latent-recurrent) language model from NVIDIA. It uses a normalized-GPT architecture with interleaved sliding-window and full attention layers. A shared block of layers is applied repeatedly, so Dory can spend more compute per token. The loop count can be changed at inference time on the same checkpoint to trade speed against quality. Links: Documentation | Paper (nGPT) Add Dory model support ( #50099 ) by @shan18 HY4-VL HY4-VL (Hunyuan V4 Vision-Language) combines the HYV4 mixture-of-experts text backbone with a vision encoder for image-text and video-text generation. It supports dynamic-resolution visual inputs and uses multimodal rotary position embeddings (mRoPE) to represent temporal and spatial positions. It builds on the Qwen2-VL design and shares its vision patch merger with HunYuan-VL. Links: Documentation Add HY4-VL ( #50877 ) by @vasqu Omnilingual ASR Omnilingual ASR is a suite of multilingual speech-recognition models from Meta FAIR that covers more than 1,600 languages. Each model pairs a Wav2Vec2-style audio encoder with one of two heads: CTC ( OmniASRForCTC ): a linear projection to the vocabulary, decoded non-autoregressively with greedy CTC. Audio language model ( OmniASRForConditionalGeneration ): audio embeddings are projected into a Llama decoder that generates the transcription. It optionally takes a language code (e.g. "eng_Latn" ), which generally improves transcription quality. Both variants come in 300M, 1B, 3B and 7B sizes. Links: Documentation | CTC Documentation | Paper Adding Omnilingual ASR models ( #43265 ) by @ebezzam Lara Mini Lara Mini is a multilingual base language model from Translated with 7.2B total and 0.6B active parameters per token. It is a hybrid of linear-time recurrent layers, sliding-window attention and a few global attention layers, each followed by a fine-grained mixture of experts. The weights are released under the CC BY-NC-SA 4.0 license (non-commercial use) in a gated repository. Links: Documentation | Paper Add Lara Mini ( #50819 ) by @ValeGian SarvamMLA SarvamMLA is the architecture of Sarvam-105B, a 105B-parameter mixture-of-experts language model from Sarvam AI. It combines Multi-head Latent Attention (MLA) with sparse MoE routing: 128 routed experts with 8 active per token, plus 1 shared expert. It uses sigmoid routing with group-based top-k selection and YaRN rotary embeddings for contexts up to 131K tokens. The architecture is the same as DeepSeek-V3, with a custom configuration. Links: Documentation Add SarvamMLA model (sarvamai/sarvam-105b) ( #44569 ) by @aashay-sarvam SarvamMoE SarvamMoE is the architecture of Sarvam-30B, Sarvam AI's 30B-parameter mixture-of-experts model. It uses grouped-query attention with QK normalization, and 128 routed experts with 6 active per token, plus 1 shared expert. The architecture is the same as GLM-4-MoE, so the auto classes load it with the GLM-4-MoE implementation and only SarvamMoEConfig is specific to SarvamMoE. Links: Documentation Add SarvamMoE (sarvamai/sarvam-30b) ( #51023 ) by @hmellor EXAONE EXAONE covers the EXAONE 3.0, EXAONE 3.5 and EXAONE Deep language models from LG AI Research. Their architecture is the same as Llama, so the auto classes load them with LlamaModel and LlamaForCausalLM , and only ExaoneConfig is specific to EXAONE. The released checkpoints are renamed to the Llama names when loading and back when saving, so they no longer need trust_remote_code=True . Links: Documentation Add EXAONE ( #50966 ) by @hmellor Model updates Ling 3.1 Flash now loads natively through BailingHybrid , like Ling 3.0 in v5.20.0 ( #49737 ) by @icavan Beam gains a BeamForTokenClassification head ( #50634 ) by @AymenKallala Breaking changes Cache renaming: past_key_values / cache_params → cache ( #50585 , #50730 ) past_key_values and cache_params are renamed to cache across the library. The old names still work with a deprecation warning; see the dedicated section below. 🚨🚨 Rename past_key_values / cache_params to cache ( #50585 ) by @Cyrilvallez Bump minimal peft version for cache name compatibility ( #50730 ) by @Cyrilvallez Attention models used to call their cache past_key_values , while Mamba-style and linear-attention models called it cache_params . Hybrid models therefore had to juggle two names for the same object. There is now a single name, cache , everywhere: model forward signatures, generate , prepare_inputs_for_generation , the masking utilities, and every ModelOutput . # Before outputs = model ( input_ids , past_key_values = past_key_values , use_cache = True ) next_cache = outputs . past_key_values # Now outputs = model ( input_ids , cache = cache , use_cache = True ) next_cache = outputs . cache Fully backward compatible for now : past_key_values= / cache_params= are renamed to cache automatically, with a one-time deprecation warning. Model forward and prepare_inputs_for_generation accept the old names until v5.40.0 , and generate accepts them until v6.0.0 . Passing both an old name and cache raises a ValueError . Outputs too : outputs.past_key_values , outputs.cache_params and outputs["past_key_values"] still return the cache. Output classes can also still be built with the old field names (e.g. CausalLMOutputWithPast(past_key_values=...) ), so most remote-code models keep working unchanged. Custom code : models defined outside the library should rename their arguments to cache . Layers now call cache.update(key_states, value_states, layer_idx, kwargs=kwargs) , so custom Cache subclasses that override update should accept the extra kwargs argument. 🚨 peft>=0.22.0 is now required. 📚 Docs: https://huggingface.co/docs/transformers/main/en/kv_cache Multimodal Outputs Generative multimodal models now return shared output classes ( MultimodalBaseModelOutputWithPast , MultimodalCausalLMOutputWithPast , and their MoE variants) instead of one output class per model. Code that checks for a model-specific output class should switch to these. 🚨 Multimodal Model Output for generative LMs ( #50379 ) by @zucchini-nlp modeling_attn_mask_utils.py has been removed. Every function in it had been deprecated in favor of transformers.masking_utils . Remote-code models that still import _prepare_4d_causal_attention_mask or AttentionMaskConverter from it must move to transformers.masking_utils . Other things Remove deprecated and unused older mask API file ( #50728 ) by @Cyrilvallez LayoutLMv3 (and the PP-DocLayoutV2 reading-order model that shares its code) now go through the attention interface, so SDPA and flex attention are supported. The relative position bias is built once per forward pass and passed to attention as position_bias . 🚨 LayoutLMv3: support SDPA through the attention interface, build the relative position bias once ( #50688 ) by @14H034160212 Cache Beyond the rename, this release adds static-cache support to assisted decoding and fixes generate with flex attention and a static cache. StaticCache now allocates values with the value states' dtype, and the cache is kept under activation checkpointing when gradients are off. The is_linear / is_croppable properties are fixed for hybrid linear/full-attention models, BigBird block-sparse decoding works with a KV cache, and KV sharing is restored for the Gemma 4 assistants. Support static cache in assisted decoding ( #49415 ) by @jiqing-feng Simplify cache handling in generate ( #50910 ) by @Cyrilvallez Fix generate with flex attention and a static cache ( #50864 ) by @tarekziade Allocate the StaticCache values with the value states' dtype ( #49554 ) by @qgallouedec Keep the cache under activation checkpointing when gradients are off ( #50890 ) by @qgallouedec [cache] Fix is_linear property to correctly remove hybrid layers ( #51030 ) by @Cyrilvallez Fix is_croppable property for mixed linear-full attention classes ( #51028 ) by @Cyrilvallez Fix BigBird block-sparse decoding with a KV cache ( #49984 ) by @jiqing-feng fix(gemma4): Restore KV sharing for the Gemma 4 assistants and their targets ( #50531 ) by @harshaljanjani Fix Dory vocabulary resizing, loop validation, and last-loop static caching ( #50982 ) by @shan18 Fix device placement in test_bc_cache_name_{forward,generate} ( #50757 ) by @ydshieh Update test_dynamic_cache_hard expected values for A10G ( #50822 ) by @ydshieh Generation Generation fixes cover sampled beam search (candidates are sorted again before finalization), constrained sampling (batch IDs are preserved), generate on MPS with encoder-decoder models, and TextStreamer , which no longer drops spaces or lags on text without spaces such as Chinese, Japanese and Korean. StopStringCriteria initializes faster, and its cache now actually hits. paper.title: llm-gemini 0.38.1
paper.abstract: Release: llm-gemini 0.38.1 Gemini 4 Carbon only supports low , medium and high reasoning levels - but Gemini 4 Hydrogen and Gemini 4 Neon both have an extra xhigh level. I missed that when I added those models to the llm-gemini plugin, which is now fixed in this dot release. The xhigh setting for Hydrogen makes a significant difference. I updated my Gemini 4 comparison grid - note how Hydrogen at high used 5,311 output tokens and cost 3.99 cents, but the same model at xhigh used 31,477 output tokens, cost 23.61 cents, and produced a pelican that's competitive with Gemini 4 Neon: Tags: gemini , llm , llm-reasoning , pelican-riding-a-bicycle , ai , llms , google , generative-ai
